**Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES**

The five bounded contracts hold on the supplied text. Ownership of the qualification bindings and the profile fixture is explicit and consistent between CORE-03 and NATIVE-01. The migration chain runs CORE-05 runner, CORE-09 guarded primitive, then NATIVE-09 and NATIVE-11 by inheritance, with OPS-05 reusing it for coordinated release migration, and the graph has no cycle through those nodes. Mechanical OPS-04 and live OPS-12 are separated so OPS-05/06/07 do not wait on live proof, and OPS-10 extends rather than first-creates the complete-slice fixtures. Three gaps remain.

**Findings**

1. **Registry population edits have no canonical owner outside CORE-01 and OPS-10.** The common paragraph requires every fixture-creating ticket to register its population in the fixed registry, and CORE-01 makes that registry reject unknown groups and unregistered populations. Yet CORE-03, CORE-05, CORE-09, CORE-10, NATIVE-01, NATIVE-02, NATIVE-09, NATIVE-11, OPS-03, OPS-04, OPS-05 and OPS-12 do not list the registry file in their canonical source changes, and only NATIVE-02 names which of the four declared groups its population belongs to. Memory records, improvement adoption, qualification, steering/accounting and remote policy populations are never mapped to installation, store, execution or complete-slice, so the OPS-10 closure commands could pass while those populations sit outside every verified group. The same omission applies to the migration runner: CORE-05 designates the canonical runner file in prose but leaves it out of its canonical list. Fix: add one sentence to the common paragraph placing registry-file edits in scope for every fixture-creating ticket and requiring each ticket to name its target group, then add the runner file to CORE-05's canonical list.

2. **Offline GPU continuation is not bounded by the shared effort reservation.** OPS-03 reserves against the CORE-10 scope before remote submit, and OPS-04 states the GPU cap is additional to the shared scope and never a fresh allowance. Nothing requires the pre-dispatch reservation to cover the job's full admitted offline envelope. While the Mac is disconnected only the runner-enforced GPU cap bounds consumption, and the single store writer cannot settle or stop anything. If the envelope exceeds the reservation, the job legally consumes beyond the shared allowance and CORE-10's "same effort allowance" guarantee fails offline. Fix: in OPS-03 or OPS-04, require that admission refuse any fixed GPU job whose declared time/resource bound exceeds its durable reservation, and add a negative case for an envelope larger than the reservation to the remote-policy population.

3. **OPS-04 host assignment is underspecified for runner-side cases.** OPS-04 says to run its population on both admitted host fixtures, but its positive evidence includes job-host lease expiry independent of the runner and native interruption at the admitted deadline, which depend on the Linux service manager. OPS-05 resolves the identical problem with an explicit role split and a rule against inferring both-host support from Mac-only runs. OPS-04 has no such split, so the acceptance either demands impossible Mac service behavior or permits Mac-only evidence for Linux runner cases, contradicting the common paragraph. Fix: copy OPS-05's host-assignment paragraph into OPS-04 and name which remote-policy cases are controller-side on both hosts versus runner-side on Linux.

**Minor note, not counted:** CORE-03 tells implementers not to duplicate ENV-01, which is not a node in the supplied graph. Replace it with the actual ticket identifier or delete the reference.

**Reviewed scope and limits**

- Reviewed only the supplied ticket texts for CORE-01/03/05/09/10, NATIVE-01/02/09/11, OPS-03/04/05/10/12, the capability graph, and the three supplied contract documents.
- Not supplied and therefore unverified: CORE-02/04/06/07/08, NATIVE-03 through 08, 10, 12, 13, OPS-01/02/06 through 09/11. Creating owners for recovery, capture, installation contracts, platform ownership and lifecycle files, which CORE-09, OPS-03 and NATIVE-02 extend, could not be confirmed.
- I did not run the local validator, verify packet hashes, inspect source files, or read any cited architecture document beyond the three contracts included here.
- All commands and tests are treated as proposed interfaces. No claim about run code is made or assessed.
